data.description:
## Context

Dogfooding capture from Brandon (2026-08-01). The generated markdown files on the `tuhdoo` data branch (backlog.md and friends, produced by internal/views) are the human-readable face of the ledger — what you see browsing the branch on a git host or catting files. Right now they're utilitarian dumps; they should be pretty, or at least easy to read and scan at a glance.

## The ask

A design pass on the generated markdown:

- Decide the reading experience first (what does someone glancing at the branch on GitHub want to see, in what order?), then shape the views to serve it: clear headings, tables where they scan better than lists, sensible ordering (actionable states before done/archived), short IDs, maybe restrained use of bold/badges. Taste over decoration.
- Keep every view deterministic and generated by pure functions (T1) — same events in, same bytes out.

## Acceptance

- Views render legibly both as raw text in a terminal and as rendered markdown on a git host.
- View generation stays pure and table-driven-testable; golden tests updated to the new output; make test lint green.
- Before/after of backlog.md in the PR description so the design change is reviewable as behavior.

## Pointers

- internal/views/views.go and its tests; the live output on the `tuhdoo` branch of this repo.

## Constraints

- Additive to the view layer only — stored event bytes are never rewritten (T3); no schema changes.
data.title: Design pass on the generated markdown views: scannable, glanceable data branch
